subject: Tenant entry & credentialing navigator — ALTIQ initial setup
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Tenant entry & credentialing navigator — ALTIQ initial setup

Hi Sam —

Congrats again on the signed agreement. Wanted to start the handoff and lay out a minimal, timeboxed onboarding sequence so your engineers can make calls against a seeded workspace this week. Attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a one‑page credentialing checklist.

High level proposal (two sprint approach):
- Sprint 1 (Days 0–3): Admin invites + project namespace creation, seed service account, generate initial API keys for dev env.
- Sprint 2 (Days 4–10): Role matrix enforcement, KMS decision + key binding (optional), rotate keys for staging, test end-to-end sample calls.

Key decisions we need from ALTIQ by EOD Wednesday:
1) Confirm primary admin user to receive organization invites (we will send owner-level invite).
2) Will you use your own KMS for secret management, or use Redwood-managed ephemeral keys?
3) Any IP allowlists or proxying that would block our provisioning calls?

Proposed kickoff time: Thursday 2025-10-12 10:00 AM PT (30m) — I included Ben and Monica to lead the technical and CS side.

Attachments: ALTIQ_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1.2.xlsx (MAP), tenant-credentialing-checklist.pdf

Next steps from Redwood: we will seed a project namespace called altiq-prod-preview, create a service account named altiq-seed-svc, and issue two short-lived API keys scoped to that project. Monica will post the detailed seeding steps to the shared drive after this thread.

Thanks — speak soon,

— Soojin

Thanks Soojin — this looks good and concise. A few clarifying items: 

- Primary admin: I'll be the initial org admin (sam.wong@altiq.com). After seeding we will add two infra engineers to the admin role.
- KMS: ALTIQ prefers to use our GCP KMS for production secrets. For the preview/dev keys we're fine with Redwood-managed short-lived keys, provided we can later bind to our KMS for prod.
- Network: We do have an outbound proxy but can open the specific endpoints you need.

Can you email the exact FQDNs/IPs the provisioning service will call so our network team can pre-authorize? Also, can we move kickoff to 11:00 AM PT — Tara (CISO) wants to join the initial KMS discussion.

Sam

Hi Sam — great, thanks for the quick reply. A couple notes from the seeding/runbook side so your network and KMS teams have exact asks: 

Provisioning endpoints (outbound):
- api.redwood.ai:443 (provisioning & management API)
- seeding.redwood-internal.net:443 (project/service-account bootstrap)
- auth.redwood.ai:443 (token exchange)

If you have strict egress rules please whitelist those FQDNs and allow TLS inspection exceptions for the provisioning window (48 hours). We will not exfiltrate secrets; keys are issued and visible only to the admin user during the initial handoff.

Seeding steps we will execute once Sam accepts the owner invite: 
1) Create workspace namespace: altiq-preview-2025
2) Create service account: altiq-seed-svc and attach minimal roles: admin.read, keys.create, projects.seed
3) Generate 2 API keys: dev-preview (30d) and integration-test (7d) — both are short-lived.
4) Post seeding artifacts: JSON manifest with project IDs, service-account email, and instruction to rotate into your KMS for prod binding.

On the KMS topic: we recommend binding to your GCP KMS for production. For the handoff we will issue keys managed by Redwood (ephemeral) but will provide an automated rotation script to push the secret into GCP KMS. Rishi will include that automation in the drive link after this thread.

I moved the kickoff to Thu 2025-10-12 11:00 AM PT in the calendar invite. Agenda (30m): intros, network/KMS checklist, walkthrough of seeding steps, immediate acceptance & invite flow.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
